pr_title: fix handling of client cert on macOS
pr_body:
We did not build X509Chain when using specific client or server certificate (e.g. Without context). 
We used to call X509Chain.Build inside of PAL but we don't any more. So the intermediate CA certificates would not be sent even if available in certificate stores. 

This got missed by the existing test. Because of #48207 the prerequisites would never be satisfied and the test would always skip on macOS. 
Also macOS can provide full chain (when certs are stored in Key Chain) even if the client did not sent everything. 

To fix both the test is no longer conditional. Hopefully it will be stable enough in CI. 

fixes #66537
contributes to #73295

issue_context.title: Intermediate Certs not being sent from client to server on MAC
issue_context.body:
### Description

I am trying to send certificates from client to the server to do a mTLS Handshake. Server expects 3 certs ( 1 Leaf + 2 Intermediates ).

I am adding leaf certificate like this in my code - 

```c#
HttpClientHandler handler = new HttpClientHandler();

handler.ClientCertificateOptions = ClientCertificateOption.Manual;
handler.SslProtocols = SslProtocols.Tls12;

var c = X509Certificate2.CreateFromPemFile(certPath, pvtKey);
handler.ClientCertificates.Add(c);

// Create an HttpClient object
httpClient = new HttpClient(handler);
```
            

 I can see on the Wireshark that only leaf certificate is written on the wire.
 I understand that it will try to automatically build the chain from OS and add intermediates.
 Both my intermediate certs have been added to System keychain - but still it will only send the leaf cert.
 This is happening on .NET Core 5.
 Platform - MAC

### Reproduction Steps

Create HttpClient with HttpClientHandler on .NET Core 5 and try to send intermediate certs along with the leaf certificate.

### Expected behavior

Client sends the complete chain to server.

### Actual behavior

Client is not able to add intermediate certs.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

_No response_

### Other information

_No response_

Yes @wfurt 
I only have partial chain with me on the client. Server will complete the chain and then verify.

I wonder if dotnet is trying to pick intermediate certs from "System Roots" keychain on Mac where even an Administrator can't add any cert.

The "System Roots"  is for trusted CAs not intermediates. I look at this again we we should basically use 
```c#
SslStreamCertificateContext.Create(c, NULL, false);
```
that use `X509Chain` under the cover. Once that build, it would be curious what that would be different. 
My assumption was that the client cannot construct the chain with intermediates. 

It may be worth of trying .NET 6 if you can. I did not see anything obvious that would make difference but it would be good to know.

I have a similar issue like @ppruthi-sfdc.

# Description
I am trying to send certificates from client to the server to do a mTLS Handshake. Server expects 2 certs (1 Leaf + 1 Intermediate) and I'm also using the HttpClientHandler to send the certificates from a pem file. 
This worked until .net 5.0.14; but stopped working with .net 5.0.15 and does not work with any .net 6.0.x version.
I can see on the Wireshark that only leaf certificate is written on the wire for .net 5.0.15/.net 6.0.x.
This is happening on .NET 5.0.15ff, .NET 6.0.0ff.
Platform - Linux Container

This issue is hindering to migrate to .NET 6.

# Expected behavior
Client sends the leaf and intermediate certificate to the server and client/server communication works.

# Actual behavior
The actual behavior was logged with Wireshark.
Client sends the leaf and intermediate certificate to the server when running in docker container mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:5.0.14 and hence the communication works.
Client sends only the leaf certificate but no intermediate to the server when running in docker container mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:6.0.6 resulting in an Unknown CA TLS error.
Client performs even no TLS handshake  when running in docker container mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:5.0.17 resulting in failing communication.

# Additional information
- the certificates of the pem file are installed in the docker container using update-ca-certificates
- .net 5.0.14 container runs "OpenSSL 1.1.1d 10 Sep 2019" whereas .net 5.0.15/.net 6.0.x containers run "OpenSSL 1.1.1n  15 Mar 2022"
- .net 5.0.14: X509Chain.Build(cert) results in 
```
ChainBuild.Status: True
ChainBuild.ElementCount: 3
```
- .net 5.0.17/.net 6.0.x: X509Chain.Build(cert) results in
```
ChainBuild.Status: False
ChainBuild.ElementCount: 1
```

While the behavior is similar this looks like distance problem @maxarm. 
@bartonjs may have some insight since it seems like you can reproduce it with simple  X509Chain.Build.
I suggest to open separate issue and post details about your intermediate certificates. 
It is certainly possible that newer OpenSSL is more picky about certificate extensions.

A diff of the v5.0.14 tag to the v5.0.15 tag shows no changes in certificate processing, so it must be something between OpenSSL 1.1.1d and 1.1.1n (or that you lost some client state during the upgrade).

As @wfurt said, it's a new problem, so should be in a new issue; but without a specific certificate that behaves differently between 5.0.14 and 5.0.15 there's no help we can provide or investigation we can do.

Thanks @wfurt and @bartonjs for your help so far.
As suggested I created a new issue https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/71825 containing additional information like certificates, code, stacktrace.

For me it's also interesting that 5.0.15/6.0.6 behave differently, though using same openssl 1.1.1n.
I extracted the critical code into a minimal application so there should be no unintended other changes leading to this issue.
